name: Andy Burnham
role: Prime Minister & First Lord of the Treasury
bio: Former Mayor of Greater Manchester (2017–2026) and cabinet minister. Elected Labour Leader on July 16, 2026, and took office as Prime Minister on July 20, 2026, following Keir Starmer's resignation.
keyStance: Establishing a National Care Service, regional devolution and Northern powerhouse investment, public ownership of water and energy, reforming long-term pension structures with a 2030 double lock.

name: Louise Haigh
role: First Secretary of State, Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster & Minister for the Cabinet Office
bio: Senior minister and de facto deputy to the Prime Minister, overseeing civil service reform, delivery of cross-government priorities, and constitutional affairs.
keyStance: Cabinet coordination, public sector productivity, transport integration, and strengthening regional devolved authorities.

name: John Healey
role: Chancellor of the Exchequer
bio: Appointed Chancellor by Andy Burnham in July 2026 to lead fiscal and economic policy, transitioning from his previous Defence brief.
keyStance: Balancing fiscal discipline with long-term infrastructure investment, protecting low-income pensioners from personal allowance tax drag, and securing funding for the National Care Service.

name: Ed Miliband
role: Secretary of State for Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Affairs
bio: Experienced former party leader appointed Foreign Secretary in July 2026, spearheading international climate diplomacy and resetting European security partnerships.
keyStance: Global climate pacts, strengthening European security cooperation and NATO alignment, diplomatic conflict resolution, and green export promotion.

name: Shabana Mahmood
role: Home Secretary
bio: Promoted to Home Secretary in July 2026 to lead law enforcement, border security, counter-terrorism, and policing integrity.
keyStance: Expanding the Border Security Command, modernizing neighbourhood policing, tackling organized immigration crime, and expediting judicial case processing.

name: Wes Streeting
role: Secretary of State for Defence
bio: Appointed Defence Secretary in July 2026, leading the Strategic Defence Review implementation, armed forces modernization, and NATO commitments.
keyStance: Meeting the 2.5% of GDP defence spending trajectory, domestic sovereign defence industrial strategy, and deepening allied defense pacts.

name: Yvette Cooper
role: Secretary of State for Health and Social Care
bio: Veteran cabinet minister leading the health brief to integrate social care with the NHS and implement Burnham's National Care Service.
keyStance: Founding the National Care Service, slashing NHS elective waiting times, community preventative care, and workforce retention.

name: Lucy Powell
role: Secretary of State for Education
bio: Key Manchester ally and long-serving education policy architect, driving early years investment and technical skills reform.
keyStance: Expanding funded early years childcare, establishing high-quality apprenticeships and vocational pathways, and funding primary school breakfast clubs.

name: Angela Rayner
role: Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government
bio: Grassroots leader spearheading regional housing delivery, workers' rights legislation, and devolution to metro mayors.
keyStance: Building 1.5M new homes, ending Section 21 no-fault evictions, local planning reform, and empowering regional mayors.

name: Kemi Badenoch
role: Leader of the Opposition & Conservative Leader
bio: Elected Conservative Party leader in November 2024. Former Business and Trade Secretary and Equalities Minister, emphasizing institutional reform, free enterprise, and rebuilding trust.
keyStance: Roll back state intervention, defend family enterprise and farming inheritance reliefs, dismantle civil service quangos, reduce welfare dependency.

name: Mel Stride
role: Shadow Chancellor of the Exchequer
bio: Former Treasury Select Committee Chair and Work and Pensions Secretary, leading forensic economic scrutiny of government budgets.
keyStance: Oppose employer National Insurance tax hikes, defend pensions triple lock, demand strict spending reductions across Whitehall departments.

name: Chris Philp
role: Shadow Home Secretary
bio: Former Policing and Crime Minister, focusing on border security, immigration deterrence, and visible neighbourhood law enforcement.
keyStance: Demand legal caps on net migration, tough custodial sentences for knife crime, restore third-country deportation deterrence.

name: Dame Priti Patel
role: Shadow Foreign Secretary
bio: Former Home Secretary and International Development Secretary, championing bilateral global trade and robust international deterrence.
keyStance: Strong deterrent posture against hostile authoritarian states, defend Atlantic security alliance, resist EU institutional realignment.

name: James Cartlidge
role: Shadow Secretary of State for Defence
bio: Former Defence Procurement Minister with deep insight into military supply chains and frontline equipment modernization.
keyStance: Legislate 2.5% of GDP defence spending by 2030, ring-fence Dreadnought nuclear submarine replacement, protect British Army headcount floor.

name: Nick Timothy
role: Shadow Secretary of State for Justice
bio: Former Downing Street Chief of Staff and prominent policy architect appointed Shadow Justice Secretary by Kemi Badenoch, succeeding Robert Jenrick following the latter's defection.
keyStance: Defending British judicial sovereignty, reforming legal aid bureaucracy, strengthening criminal sentencing guidelines, and expanding custodial capacity.

name: Claire Coutinho
role: Shadow Secretary of State for Energy Security and Net Zero
bio: Former Energy Secretary, leading the Conservative critique of Great British Energy and green levies on household bills.
keyStance: Annual North Sea oil and gas licensing, Small Modular Nuclear Reactors (SMRs), oppose rapid green mandates that inflate domestic bills.

name: Victoria Atkins
role: Shadow Secretary of State for Health and Social Care
bio: Former Secretary of State for Health and Financial Secretary to the Treasury, leading the opposition's scrutiny of NHS productivity and hospital modernization.
keyStance: Demanding operational NHS productivity audits, opposing unfunded public sector union pay awards, and expanding community pharmacy services.

name: Laura Trott
role: Shadow Secretary of State for Education
bio: Former Chief Secretary to the Treasury and Pensions Minister, spearheading scrutiny of school standards, apprenticeship funding, and university finance.
keyStance: Protecting rigorous academic standards, opposing VAT on independent school fees, and redirecting underperforming degree funds to technical colleges.

name: Nigel Farage
role: Party Leader & MP
bio: Leader of Reform UK and MP for Clacton, who unveiled the party's first official 'Shadow Cabinet' team in February 2026 to signal readiness for government.
keyStance: Freeze non-essential immigration, leave the ECHR, raise personal income tax allowance to £20,000, scrap Net Zero subsidies, and introduce private-public healthcare competition.

name: Richard Tice
role: Deputy Leader & Shadow Secretary of State for Business, Trade and Energy
bio: Deputy Leader appointed to the Business, Trade and Energy brief in February 2026, leading deregulation and industrial economic policy.
keyStance: Cut corporation tax to 15%, lift employer National Insurance thresholds, fast-track North Sea gas and UK shale extraction, and scrap all green levies.

name: Robert Jenrick
role: Shadow Chancellor of the Exchequer
bio: Former Conservative leadership contender and immigration minister who defected to Reform UK, appointed Shadow Chancellor by Nigel Farage in February 2026.
keyStance: Aggressive government spending restraint, abolition of family farm and business inheritance tax, reversing employer National Insurance rises, and lowering fuel duties.

name: Zia Yusuf
role: Shadow Home Secretary
bio: Tech entrepreneur and Reform UK Party Chairman appointed Shadow Home Secretary in February 2026 to lead border enforcement and immigration policy.
keyStance: Immediate offshore processing and returns for illegal arrivals, leaving the ECHR and Refugee Convention, mass deportations of foreign offenders, and strict work visa quotas.

name: Suella Braverman
role: Shadow Secretary of State for Education, Skills and Equalities
bio: Former Home Secretary and Attorney General who defected to Reform UK, appointed to lead education, skills, and institutional reform in Farage's frontbench team.
keyStance: Scrapping diversity and equality civil service mandates, defending traditional curriculum standards, promoting technical trade apprenticeships, and protecting freedom of speech.

name: Lee Anderson
role: Chief Whip & Working Class Champion
bio: Former coal miner and deputy party chairman serving as Parliamentary Chief Whip, spearheading working-class voter mobilization and party discipline.
keyStance: Zero tolerance on illegal channel crossings, defunding migrant hotel contracts, tough criminal sentencing, and protecting red-wall industrial jobs.

name: Danny Kruger
role: Head of Preparation for Government & Policy
bio: Leading conservative intellectual and author who joined Reform UK's parliamentary apparatus to head preparations for executive government and legislative drafting.
keyStance: Systemic civil service restructuring, restoring parliamentary sovereignty, institutional reform of regulatory bodies, and local community revitalization.

name: Rupert Lowe
role: Spokesperson for Business, Agriculture & Deregulation
bio: Businessman and former football club chairman campaigning against Whitehall red tape and the regulatory burden on British farming and fishing.
keyStance: Cutting Whitehall administrative staffing by 50%, full protection for agricultural inheritance reliefs, and restoring British coastal fishing rights.

name: Sir Ed Davey
role: Party Leader & MP
bio: Former Energy Secretary who led the Liberal Democrats to a historic 72 MPs in 2024, focusing on health, social care, carer support, and public service renewal.
keyStance: Universal access to GP appointments within 7 days, £5bn free personal adult social care package, ban water executive bonuses, and establish a long-term pathway back to the EU Single Market.

name: Daisy Cooper
role: Deputy Leader & Treasury Spokesperson
bio: Deputy Leader and former Health Spokesperson, leading the Lib Dem economic scrutiny on equitable taxation and public service reinvestment.
keyStance: Windfall tax on energy super-profits, higher levies on big tech monopolies, unfreezing tax allowances, and targeted support for high street small businesses.

name: Helen Morgan
role: Spokesperson for Health and Social Care
bio: Chartered accountant and by-election victor leading parliamentary campaigns against rural ambulance wait times, hospital corridor care, and dental deserts.
keyStance: Dedicated emergency funding for ambulance response times, mental health parity across all NHS trusts, and free personal social care for all adults.

name: Calum Miller
role: Spokesperson for Foreign Affairs
bio: Former senior civil servant with deep international diplomacy and foreign policy background, leading scrutiny of international treaties.
keyStance: Rebuilding UK-EU institutional partnerships, steadfast support for Ukraine, upholding international law, and restoring the 0.7% foreign aid budget.

name: Munira Wilson
role: Spokesperson for Education, Children and Families
bio: Leading national voice on education and child welfare, championing free school meals and youth mental health support in all schools.
keyStance: Extend free school meals to all primary school pupils living in poverty, fund a qualified mental health specialist in every school, and reform special educational needs (SEND) provision.

name: Tim Farron
role: Spokesperson for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
bio: Former party leader and veteran rural champion leading the national campaign against raw sewage dumping in British lakes and rivers.
keyStance: Transform water companies into public benefit entities, legally ban water executive bonuses until sewage dumping ends, and protect British family farmers.

name: Sarah Olney
role: Spokesperson for Business and Trade
bio: Former accountant leading scrutiny on industrial policy, regulatory barriers, and high street revitalization.
keyStance: Scrap and replace the broken business rates system with a commercial landowner levy, negotiate veterinary and trade pacts with Europe, and boost green export finance.

name: Max Wilkinson
role: Spokesperson for Home Affairs
bio: Elected in 2024 to lead home affairs, police accountability, and community safety policy.
keyStance: Restore dedicated community neighbourhood policing, clear the asylum backlog with faster case-processing units, and reform drug enforcement laws.

name: James MacCleary
role: Spokesperson for Defence
bio: Experienced local leader elected in 2024 leading defence procurement scrutiny and Armed Forces personnel welfare.
keyStance: Reach 2.5% of GDP defence spending responsibly, strengthen European NATO pillar, reverse troop cuts, and legally enshrine the Armed Forces Covenant.

name: Pippa Heylings
role: Spokesperson for Energy Security and Net Zero
bio: International environmental expert leading the Lib Dem transition roadmap to clean renewable power.
keyStance: Accelerate community rooftop solar, upgrade national grid infrastructure, insulate millions of fuel-poor homes, and ban new fossil fuel extraction.

name: Wendy Chamberlain
role: Chief Whip & Spokesperson for Scotland
bio: Former police officer and long-serving parliamentary leader managing party discipline and parliamentary procedure.
keyStance: Strict parliamentary standards, banning MP second jobs, electoral reform via proportional representation, and stronger Scottish devolution.

name: Zack Polanski
role: Party Leader
bio: Elected Leader of the Green Party of England and Wales in September 2025, succeeding Carla Denyer & Adrian Ramsay. Prominent London Assembly Member and national campaigner for wealth redistribution, electoral reform, and climate justice.
keyStance: Universal Basic Income trials, immediate proportional representation for Westminster, an annual 2% wealth tax on fortunes over £10m, and an immediate statutory halt to all new fossil fuel extraction.

name: Carla Denyer
role: Parliamentary Leader & MP
bio: Renewable energy engineer elected MP for Bristol Central in 2024. Following her co-leadership (2021–2025), she leads the 4-member Green parliamentary group in the House of Commons, focusing on public healthcare and progressive taxation.
keyStance: Annual 1% to 2% wealth tax on assets over £10m, statutory municipal rent controls, reversal of NHS privatisation, and scrapping Trident.

name: Adrian Ramsay
role: Parliamentary Spokesperson for Environment, Rural Affairs & Utilities & MP
bio: Environmental strategist elected MP for rural Waveney Valley in 2024 (former co-leader 2021–2025), leading Green parliamentary work on rural infrastructure, agricultural transition, and river health.
keyStance: Protect British biodiversity, bring water monopolies and National Grid into public ownership, halt new oil and gas, and restore rural bus networks.

name: Ellie Chowns
role: Parliamentary Spokesperson for Economy, Food & Agriculture & MP
bio: Former MEP and international development specialist elected MP for North Herefordshire in 2024, leading Green scrutiny on trade agreements, agricultural subsidies, and rural river health.
keyStance: Transform agricultural subsidies to reward regenerative farming, enforce strict phosphate limits on industrial poultry units, and progressive ecological tax reform.

name: Siân Berry
role: Parliamentary Spokesperson for Transport, Housing & Democracy & MP
bio: Former London Assembly Member and veteran green campaigner elected MP for Brighton Pavilion in 2024, succeeding Caroline Lucas.
keyStance: Universal rent controls, massive council house construction, public ownership of buses and railways, and votes for 16-year-olds with proportional representation.

name: Mothin Ali
role: Deputy Leader (Communities & Urban Regeneration)
bio: Elected Green Party Deputy Leader in August 2025; community gardener and Leeds councillor campaigning on urban poverty, youth services, and community empowerment.
keyStance: Community wealth building, radical investment in disadvantaged inner-city areas, and vocal anti-austerity campaigning.

name: Rachel Millward
role: Deputy Leader (Local Government & Climate Action)
bio: Elected Green Party Deputy Leader in August 2025; leader of the Alliance for Wealden Council and climate organizer promoting grassroots municipal transition.
keyStance: Decentralised municipal solar and insulation, rural public transport restoration, and empowering local councils with statutory green planning powers.

name: John Swinney
role: Party Leader & First Minister of Scotland
bio: First Minister of Scotland and veteran statesman leading the Scottish Government with focus on child poverty reduction and public services.
keyStance: Scottish self-determination, scrap the two-child benefit cap across the UK, remove Trident nuclear weapons from Scotland, rejoin EU.

name: Stephen Flynn
role: Westminster Parliamentary Group Leader & MP
bio: Leading SNP parliamentarian driving parliamentary scrutiny of energy transition, Scottish budget consequentials, and cost of living.
keyStance: Just transition for North Sea energy workers without cliff-edges, demand full devolution of employment and migration powers.

name: Kirsty Blackman
role: Westminster Spokesperson for Work, Pensions & Cabinet Office
bio: Experienced Westminster frontbencher holding the UK government to account on welfare reform, pensions indexation, and civil service oversight.
keyStance: Defend the pensions triple lock, repeal punitive universal credit sanctions, and protect disability welfare entitlements from arbitrary cuts.

name: Dave Doogan
role: Westminster Spokesperson for Foreign Affairs, Defence & Trade
bio: Prominent defence and foreign policy spokesperson championing international humanitarian law, Scottish export industries, and armed forces accommodation standards.
keyStance: Re-entry into European single market arrangements, opposing overseas military escalation without parliamentary votes, and safeguarding Scottish Scotch and food exports.

name: Rhun ap Iorwerth
role: Party Leader & Member of the Senedd
bio: Former BBC journalist and Plaid Cymru leader, uniting the party around fair funding formulas, Welsh NHS renewal, and independence.
keyStance: Replace Barnett formula with needs-based funding (+£1.2bn/yr), reclaim £4bn HS2 rail consequentials, devolve Crown Estate to Wales.

name: Liz Saville Roberts
role: Westminster Group Leader & MP
bio: Privy Councillor and Westminster leader campaigning for judicial devolution and equal constitutional status for Wales.
keyStance: Devolution of policing and criminal justice to Wales, renewable energy wealth retention for Welsh communities, and constitutional fairness.

name: Ben Lake
role: Westminster Spokesperson for Treasury, Energy & Rural Affairs
bio: Respected parliamentary orator and committee member leading Plaid Cymru's financial and agricultural policy in Westminster.
keyStance: Fair agricultural funding guaranteed post-Brexit, targeted energy bill support for off-gas grid rural households, and reforming UK fiscal rules.

name: Ann Davies
role: Westminster Spokesperson for Environment, Food & Farming
bio: Farmer and local government leader elected MP for Caerfyrddin in 2024, championing family farming communities and Welsh agricultural produce.
keyStance: Protecting family farm inheritance reliefs, imposing strict origin labelling on supermarket meat and dairy, and securing clean river standards.

name: Llinos Medi
role: Westminster Spokesperson for Health, Social Care & Communities
bio: Former Council Leader elected MP for Ynys Môn in 2024, focusing on rural health inequalities, community regeneration, and youth retention in Welsh heartlands.
keyStance: Targeted funding to recruit rural NHS specialists, community housing trusts for local families, and expanding Welsh language educational provision.

name: Movement Council Executive
role: National Convenor & Constitutional Lead
bio: Civic assembly representing traditionalist British restoration, civil liberties, and free-market constitutionalism.
keyStance: Abolish Net Zero statutes, repeal legislation eroding free speech, constitutional referendums, national industrial revival.

name: Civic Campaign Spokesperson
role: Director of Policy & Enterprise
bio: Independent-minded enterprise advocate campaigning across civic forums for constitutional reform, British sovereign fishing, and deregulation.
keyStance: Radical Whitehall downsizing, dismantling regulatory quangos, repealing onerous Net Zero mandates, and defending family businesses.
